text.p: These are the leading stories in the Namibian press on Thursday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- The Uutapi magistrates court in northern Namibia cleared Deputy Minister of Environment and Tourism Nangolo Ithete of illegally purchasing ostriches and ostrich eggs. Although the maximum fines for such offences is only N$300, the case raised interest because it was the first time since independence that a senior political figure appeared in court on criminal charges.

- Several community groups in Namibia have declared their solidarity with the San demonstrators who on Sunday protested against the disposession of their ancestral lands at the gates of the Etosha National park. The groups condemned police action against the San protestors after 73 were jailed, of whom 21 remain in police custody.

- Further increases in the price of cars can be expected given the possibility of a continuing decline in the value of the South African rand, according to the chairman of the Namibian Motor Industry Federation. Remy Moens' comments follow price increases of between 3-5 percent at some local car dealers.

- The drought is losing its grip after good rainfall was recorded in most parts of the country over the last two days, with the biggest measured downpours occurring in the Leonardville district with 160mm.
- Namibian participation in the Angolan Peace Mission, UNAVEM III, will continue at least until July, the Defence Ministry said, The participation had been scheduled to end tomorrow.
